Overview

At SCA Health, we believe health care is about people – the patients we serve, the physicians we support and the teammates who push us forward. Behind every successful facility, procedure or innovation is a team of 15,000+ professionals working together, learning from each other and living out the mission, vision and values that define our organization.

As part of Optum, SCA Health is redefining specialty care by developing more accessible, patient-centered practice solutions for a network of more than 370 ambulatory surgical centers, over 400 specialty physician practice clinics and numerous labs and surgical hospitals. Our work spans a broad spectrum of services, all designed to support physicians, health systems and employers in delivering efficient, value-based care to patients without compromising quality or autonomy.

What sets SCA Health apart isn’t just what we do, it’s how we do it. Each decision we make is rooted in seven core values:

  • Clinical quality
  • Integrity
  • Service excellence
  • Teamwork
  • Accountability
  • Continuous improvement
  • Inclusion

Our values aren’t empty words – they inform our attitudes, actions and culture. At SCA Health, your work directly impacts patients, physicians and communities. Here, you’ll find opportunities to build your career alongside a team that values your expertise, invests in your success, and shares a common mission to care for patients, serve physicians and improve health care in America.

At SCA Health, we offer a comprehensive benefits package to support your health, well-being, and financial future. Our offerings include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k plan with company match, paid time off, life and disability insurance, and more. Please visit, to learn more about our benefits.

Your ideas should inspire change. If you join our team, they will.


Responsibilities

Director, Culture, Engagement & Inclusion

Transform Culture. Strengthen Engagement. Shape the Teammate Experience.

At SCA Health, we are committed to building a high-performing, purpose-driven culture where teammates feel connected, included, and empowered to do their best work. We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Director, Culture, Engagement & Inclusion to lead our enterprise approach to organizational culture, employee engagement, inclusion, and the overall teammate experience. This role will help bring our OneTeam culture to life across the organization and strengthen organizational health through data-driven insights, scalable programs, and meaningful partnerships with leaders.

Position Overview

Reporting to the Senior Director, Organizational Effectiveness, the Director, Culture, Engagement & Inclusion will serve as the enterprise leader responsible for culture strategy, employee engagement, inclusion, organizational health, and enterprise listening initiatives. This role partners closely with executive leaders, HR Business Partners, Talent Management, Leadership Development, Internal Communications, and business leaders to create a workplace experience that drives performance, retention, collaboration, and inclusion.

This role supports culture, engagement, and inclusion strategies impacting approximately 20,000 teammates across the organization.

What You'll Do

Lead Enterprise Culture Strategy

  • Partner with Organizational Effectiveness leadership to develop and execute the enterprise culture strategy aligned with business priorities.
  • Establish and monitor measures of culture effectiveness.
  • Translate OneTeam aspirations into scalable practices and experiences that reinforce desired leadership behaviors and performance expectations.
  • Drive initiatives that strengthen employee connection, organizational effectiveness, and teammate experience.

Own Employee Engagement & Listening

  • Lead the enterprise listening strategy, including the Employee Experience & Inclusion (EXI) Survey, pulse surveys, focus groups, and other listening channels.
  • Identify engagement trends, organizational risks, and opportunities.
  • Translate employee feedback into enterprise priorities and actionable recommendations.
  • Equip leaders and HR Business Partners with tools, playbooks, and resources to effectively address engagement opportunities.
  • Measure progress and impact against engagement goals.

Advance Inclusion Across the Organization

  • Develop and execute an enterprise inclusion strategy aligned to business and culture priorities.
  • Integrate inclusion practices into talent management, leadership development, onboarding, recognition, and employee experience processes.
  • Partner across Human Resources to embed inclusive leadership and decision-making into everyday practices.
  • Monitor inclusion-related measures and recommend actions that strengthen organizational effectiveness and teammate experience.

Drive Culture and Change Initiatives

  • Lead enterprise-wide culture initiatives that support organizational transformation and strategic priorities.
  • Develop change and communication strategies that reinforce desired behaviors and culture outcomes.
  • Partner with Organizational Effectiveness leaders and senior executives to support successful adoption of change initiatives.
  • Facilitate leadership conversations that strengthen alignment, culture, and organizational performance.

Deliver Organizational Insights

  • Analyze engagement, culture, inclusion, and retention data to identify trends and opportunities.
  • Develop executive dashboards and organizational health reporting.
  • Benchmark organizational practices against leading external organizations.
  • Translate data and insights into practical business recommendations for leaders and executives.

Build Strong Cross-Functional Partnerships

  • Partner with Leadership Development to align leadership capabilities and behaviors with culture priorities.
  • Collaborate with Talent Management to integrate culture and inclusion into performance management, succession planning, talent reviews, and career development.
  • Work closely with HR Business Partners, People Analytics, HR Technology, Communications, and business leaders to drive enterprise impact.

Qualifications

What You'll Bring

Required Experience

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in organizational effectiveness, culture, employee engagement, organizational development, human resources, inclusion, talent management, or related fields.
  • Experience leading enterprise-wide culture or employee engagement initiatives.
  • Demonstrated success influencing and partnering with senior leaders.
  • Experience developing strategies informed by employee insights, data, and organizational diagnostics.
  • Experience leading complex change and transformation initiatives.

Knowledge & Expertise

Strong knowledge of:

  • Organizational culture and organizational health
  • Employee engagement and employee listening strategies
  • Inclusion and belonging
  • Organizational development and effectiveness
  • Leadership effectiveness
  • Change management
  • HR strategy and workforce trends
  • People analytics and workforce insights
  • Emerging applications of AI and technology in employee experience and organizational effectiveness

Key Skills

  • Strategic consulting and business partnership
  • Strategy development and execution
  • Executive facilitation and influence
  • Survey design and interpretation
  • Data storytelling and executive communication
  • Program and change leadership
  • Stakeholder management and collaboration
  • Communication strategy and executive presentations
  • Organizational diagnostics and problem solving

You'll Thrive in This Role If You Can

  • Influence senior leaders without direct authority.
  • Translate employee insights into enterprise strategies.
  • Build trusted relationships across functions and levels.
  • Balance strategic thinking with operational execution.
  • Facilitate complex organizational discussions.
  • Turn data into action and measurable outcomes.
  • Navigate ambiguity while driving meaningful change.

Measures of Success

Success in this role will include:

  • Improvements in enterprise engagement and organizational health metrics.
  • Successful execution of the annual EXI Survey and enterprise listening strategy.
  • Increased leader adoption of engagement action planning.
  • Integration of inclusion into talent and leadership practices.
  • Delivery of actionable executive insights and culture reporting.
  • Advancement of OneTeam culture behaviors across the organization.

Why Join SCA Health?

This is a unique opportunity to shape the future culture of a growing healthcare organization, influence senior leaders, and drive meaningful impact across an enterprise of approximately 20,000 teammates. You will help create the environment, leadership practices, and employee experiences that enable our people—and our business—to thrive.

jobs.excerpt: Patent Data Specialist (Enrichment Quality & AI Readiness) Do you enjoy working hands-on with messy patent data, using SQL, Python and AI tools?
jobs.description:
Patent Data Specialist (Enrichment Quality & AI Readiness)

Do you enjoy working hands-on with messy patent data, using SQL, Python and AI tools?

Do you revel in finding the root cause of an error, then making sure it never happens again?

Come join us and help build the world's most trusted patent data, ready for the AI that professionals worldwide rely on.

About the team:


LexisNexis Intellectual Property, part of RELX, helps the world's innovators, IP professionals, law firms, and investors understand patents: their own, their competitors', and those of the companies they are assessing. Our products, including PatentSight+, IPlytics and TotalPatent One, and the patent data we deliver directly into customers' own systems, inform decisions on R&D investment, licensing, litigation, M&A and competitive strategy.

Every one of those decisions rests on the same foundation: patent data that is grouped, attributed, and kept up to date correctly. We are looking for someone who wants to help get that foundation right.

About the role:


Patent data is hard for people and machines alike. One invention can be filed in dozens of countries under different numbers and rules; one company can hold patents under many names, subsidiaries, and spellings; and whether a patent is still alive depends on events spread across years and jurisdictions. Any data or AI system built on top is only as good as the answers to a few basic questions. Which filings belong to the same family? Who really owns a patent once subsidiaries, acquisitions and spelling variants are untangled? Is a patent still in force, and do we know this for every country we are interested in? A single wrongly grouped family or misattributed owner can quietly change how a customer sees a competitor.

In this role, you will work alongside senior patent data experts to define what correct looks like for these foundations, test our data against it, and track down why things go wrong. It is a rare chance to combine patent knowledge with hands-on data work, and to grow into a recognised expert in an area that underpins everything we do.

Key Responsibilities:


  • Work with our senior patent data experts to define and maintain governed quality standards and acceptance criteria for patent families, ownership, legal status, and coverage, including how to handle tricky edge cases.
  • Build and maintain versioned test sets and worked examples, such as correctly grouped families or correctly resolved owners, that engineering teams build closed-loop evaluations on, so data quality is checked automatically and continuously.
  • Analyse our data to find quality problems, investigate their root causes with engineering teams, recommend fixes, and help design checks so they do not recur.
  • Lead smaller quality-improvement projects end to end, with support from senior colleagues.
  • Assess the quality of data from new sources and patent authorities before and after it enters our platform.
  • Review the output of automated and AI-assisted enrichment, such as ownership mapping, and feed what you learn back into the standards and evaluations.
  • Document rules and decisions clearly so they can be applied consistently, by people and by automated tools, including agentic workflows.
  • Help resolve data questions raised by product teams and customers, sometimes against tight timelines, and turn recurring ones into reusable guidance.
  • Present findings to colleagues and stakeholders

Requirements:


  • Experience working with patent data or patent information, for example as a patent analyst, patent information specialist, searcher, or in a data role at a patent office, data provider, or IP firm.
  • Understanding of how patent data is structured: families, priority claims, kind codes, legal status, assignees, and the differences between patent authorities.
  • Hands-on data skills: you are comfortable querying and analysing data yourself, for example in SQL, Python, or similar tools.
  • A methodical approach to data quality: spotting anomalies, finding root causes and checking that fixes work.
  • Practical use of AI tools in your own work beyond basic chat, for example AI-assisted data analysis, coding assistants or automated extraction, and an understanding of where automated and AI-based enrichment can go wrong.
  • Precision and care with detail, combined with the judgment to know which problems matter most.
  • Clear written communication: you can explain a data rule or an edge case so others can apply it.

Experience and education.


  • Typically, 2 or more years in patent information, patent analysis, or data roles involving patents or similarly complex data.
  • A degree in a scientific, engineering, technical, information science or related subject, or equivalent practical experience


It would be great if you also have.


  • Experience with company ownership data, corporate hierarchies, or entity resolution
  • Experience with non-English patent data, for example Chinese, Japanese or Korean
  • Familiarity with data modelling, taxonomies, or classification systems
  • Experience with data quality tooling or automated testing of data

You do not need to have worked for a data or software company before. We will help you learn how our platform works; you bring curiosity, rigour, and a feel for patent data.


This role is probably not for you if you'd rather analyse patents for specific end clients than work on the data behind the analysis, if you don't enjoy working hands-on with data, or if you're not keen to use AI tools in your work.

Why Join Us?

You'll help make sure the data behind patent decisions worldwide is right, learning from experienced experts, with the backing of a global group that has been building data, analytics and AI products for many years, and with colleagues who care about getting things right.


In your application


Please tell us briefly about one of the following:

  • A time you found an error in patent data or other complex data: how you spotted it, what caused it, and what you'd put in place to stop it happening again.
  • A time you used an AI tool on a complex data analysis task, or to parse complex data: where it helped, where it got things wrong, and how you checked.

Work in a way that works for you

We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organization. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals.


· Working flexible hours - flexing the times when you work in the day to help you fit everything in and work when you are the most productive.

Working for you


We know that your well-being and happiness are key to a long and successful career. These are some of the benefits we are delighted to offer:

  • Generous holiday allowance with the option to buy additional days.
  • Health screening, eye care vouchers, and private medical benefits
  • Wellbeing programs
  • Life assurance
  • Access to a competitive contributory pension scheme
  • Save As You Earn share option scheme.
  • Maternity, paternity, and shared parental leave
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Access to employee resource groups with dedicated time to volunteer.
  • Access to extensive learning and development resources
  • Access to employee discounts scheme via Perks at Work

About the business -


At LexisNexis Intellectual Property (LNIP), we believe that whenever a person works on a patent and understands the future trajectory of a specific technology, that person has the potential to fundamentally change how society operates. We are proud to directly support and serve these innovators in their endeavors to better humankind. We enable innovators to accomplish more by helping them make informed decisions, be more productive, comply with regulations, and ultimately achieve superior results. By harnessing the latest advances in machine learning combined with expert analysis, LexisNexis Intellectual Property is disrupting how actionable insight is extracted from patent data. Information can now be accessed with efficiency, accuracy and at a speed that is just not possible by traditional methods. Our overall success is measured by how well we deliver these results

Compensation: $34 - $36 per hour, depending on experience.

Benefits are subject to applicable eligibility requirements and plan terms.

jobs.title: Junior CRO & Shop-Konzeption Berater (m/w/d) · Remote
jobs.excerpt: Du siehst bei E-Commerce-Brands im Shop und auf Landingpages sofort, wo Optimierungspotenzial steckt?
jobs.description:
Du siehst bei E-Commerce-Brands im Shop und auf Landingpages sofort, wo Optimierungspotenzial steckt? Du willst in deiner neuen Stelle Onlineshops und Funnels entwickeln, die messbar mehr Umsatz und mehr Kunden bringen? Dann starte deine CRO-Karriere bei EVOLVE Digital.

Über EVOLVE

Wir sind ein ganzheitlicher Wachstumspartner für E-Commerce-Brands im DACH-Raum. Jedes Jahr verwalten wir über 60 Millionen € Adspend und denken jedes Projekt von der Ad über den Funnel bis zur Marge. Unser Name ist Programm: Wir entwickeln uns, unsere Dienstleistung und unsere Kunden ständig weiter. Das spiegelt sich auch in unserer Mitarbeiterbewertung auf kununu mit 4,8 von 5 Sternen wider.

Haben wir dein Interesse geweckt? Dann schau dir an, was dich bei uns erwartet.

Das wirst du tun

Gemeinsam mit unserem Team sorgst du für verkaufsstarke Shopseiten und Funnels, mit denen unsere Kunden den Markt outperformen.

  • Analyse: Du analysierst Onlineshops und Landingpages im Hinblick auf UX, Struktur, Inhalt und Marktumfeld und leitest daraus priorisierte Optimierungshypothesen ab

  • Customer Journey: Du findest Schwachstellen in der Customer Journey, belegt durch Daten und Nutzerverhalten

  • Positionierung: Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit unserem Team Positionierungen, die Marken einzigartig machen

  • Konzeption: Du erstellst Shop- und Landingpage-Konzepte inklusive Checklisten und Leitfäden, in enger Zusammenarbeit mit UX-Design und Copywriting

  • Kunden und Projekte: Du begleitest Kunden durch den Optimierungsprozess und übernimmst nach und nach das Projektmanagement

  • Trends: Du verfolgst die aktuellsten Trends im Brand- und Direct-Response-Marketing und bringst neue Ideen ins Team ein

Deine Rolle und deine Ressourcen: Du wächst Schritt für Schritt in die Rolle hinein, zuerst mit Begleitung, später eigenständig. An deiner Seite stehen erfahrene Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus CRO, UX-Design und Copywriting, die dich einarbeiten und dir regelmäßig Feedback geben. Dich erwarten flache Hierarchien, eine wertschätzende Atmosphäre und eine offene Feedbackkultur.

Das bringst du mit

  • Erste praktische Erfahrung in E-Commerce, UX oder Online-Marketing

  • Grundlegendes Verständnis für Conversion-Optimierung und A/B-Testing

  • Neugier auf E-Commerce, Marken und darauf, warum Menschen kaufen

  • Analytisches Denken: Du ordnest Beobachtungen und Zahlen ein und ziehst klare Schlüsse

  • Struktur und Eigenverantwortung: Du priorisierst und hältst Deadlines

  • Klare, verständliche Kommunikation, besonders schriftlich

  • Von Vorteil: Grundkenntnisse in GA4, Shopify, Figma, Hotjar/Clarity oder Google Workspace

Der Rahmen

  • 100 % Remote, kein Hybrid-Kompromiss

  • Vollzeit mit einer 38-Stunden-Woche

  • 30 Tage Urlaub

  • Zweimal jährlich Team-Events und Workations

  • Wöchentliche Team-Recaps und Coffee Chats, damit Remote nicht heißt, den ganzen Tag allein zu arbeiten

  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, JobRad und Firmenfitness über Wellpass

  • Steuerfreier Sachbezug von 50 € monatlich als Gutschein deiner Wahl

  • Laptop deiner Wahl und hochwertige Homeoffice-Ausstattung

  • Weiterbildungsbudget sowie interne und externe Quellen und Mentoren an deiner Seite

  • Voller Zugriff auf unseren internen AI-Stack

Vielleicht fragst du dich gerade …

„Reicht meine Erfahrung für den Einstieg?“ Wenn du schon praktisch mit E-Commerce, UX oder Online-Marketing gearbeitet hast und dich Zahlen nicht abschrecken, ja. Unsere CRO-Methodik bringen wir dir bei, die Denkweise bringst du mit.

„Ich kenne noch nicht alle Tools.“ Musst du nicht. Grundkenntnisse helfen dir, den Rest lernst du bei uns. Und ChatGPT und Claude werden schnell deine besten Freunde, denn mit den modernsten AI-Workflows optimierst du deine Arbeit und das Ergebnis für unsere Kunden. Entscheidend ist, dass du verstehen willst, was hinter den Zahlen steckt.

„Remote, bin ich da allein?“ Nein. Wir sind eine Remote-Agentur, aber Persönlichkeit und Teamspirit bleiben erhalten. Du hast das Gefühl eines Office-Teams, nur ohne Lärm und ohne Fahrt ins Büro. Dafür sorgen regelmäßige Projektabstimmungen, unsere wöchentlichen Team-Recaps und Coffee Chats. Und gerade am Anfang bekommst du regelmäßig Feedback von deinen Kolleginnen und Kollegen.

Deine Ansprechpartnerin

Vanessa, unsere HR-Managerin, ist dein erster Kontakt und freut sich auf deine Bewerbung.

jobs.excerpt: Job SummaryThe Legal Services Liaison is a multifaceted, client-facing Operations role responsible for coordinating, overseeing, and developing Dane Street’s Legal Services offerings, with primary accountability for the counter affidavit process.
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Legal Services Liaison is a multifaceted, client-facing Operations role responsible for coordinating, overseeing, and developing Dane Street’s Legal Services offerings, with primary accountability for the counter affidavit process. Acting as the primary Operations contact for legal services clients, the Liaison connects clients, attorneys, adjusters, physician reviewers, Sales, Management, and internal teams to ensure accurate, complete, timely, and professional service delivery. The role requires independent judgment and ownership across case assessment, expert selection, quality assurance, legal documentation, testimony and deposition coordination, fee management, and workflow oversight, while balancing complex legal and clinical requirements, competing deadlines, and client expectations.

Beyond daily operations, the Liaison plays a key role in strengthening client relationships, resolving service issues, ensuring report accuracy and completeness, and identifying opportunities to enhance service delivery and revenue growth. Working closely with the Operations Manager of Legal Services, Sales, and leadership, this position supports client retention, service-line development, process improvements, and evolving business needs. Success requires accountability, sound decision-making, collaboration, and a proactive, solutions-oriented approach focused on operational excellence, client satisfaction, and the continued growth of Dane Street’s Legal Services.

Mission, Culture, and Values

At Dane Street, we believe exceptional employee experiences create exceptional client experiences. Our culture is built on collaboration, continuous improvement, accountability, and care.

We care for our customers, we care for our employees, and we care for one another. Every team member plays an important role in creating an environment where people feel respected, supported, empowered to grow, and inspired to do meaningful work.

What You'll Do

Legal Case Management & Expert Coordination

  • Oversee the intake, assessment, and coordination of Legal Services cases, with primary accountability for the counter affidavit process.
  • Evaluate case requirements, identify appropriate service lines, and coordinate qualified medical experts to ensure accurate, complete, and timely deliverables that meet client expectations and applicable jurisdictional requirements.

Client Relationship Management & Service Delivery

  • Serve as the primary Operations contact for Legal Services clients and manage client relationships throughout the service delivery process.
  • Partner with attorneys, adjusters, physicians, Sales, and internal teams to address client needs and resolve escalations.
  • Communicate case progress and ensure a consistent, high-quality client experience.

Legal Documentation, Quality Assurance & Compliance

  • Oversee the quality and accuracy of legal reports, counter affidavits, testimony packages, physician credentials, and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure deliverables align with client instructions, company standards, and applicable legal and jurisdictional requirements.
  • Maintain awareness of relevant legal developments and coordinate updates to templates, workflows, and training as needed.

Operational & Workflow Oversight

  • Provide operational oversight across Legal Services, including case assignments, turnaround times, testimony and deposition coordination, urgent requests, and outstanding deliverables.
  • Identify workflow challenges and manage competing priorities.
  • Collaborate with Operations leadership to improve efficiency, maintain accountability, and support consistent service delivery.

Financial Oversight & Service Issue Resolution

  • Support the financial and administrative aspects of Legal Services, including fee schedules, case estimates, and expert fees.
  • Review and address billing discrepancies, including improperly bundled, unbundled, duplicate, or redundant charges.
  • Exercise sound judgment in addressing service concerns, pricing questions, and operational conflicts.
  • Partner with Finance, Sales, and leadership to protect client relationships and maintain business objectives.

Service-Line Development & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Sales, the Operations Manager of Legal Services, and leadership to support client retention and new business opportunities.
  • Identify opportunities to expand service offerings and strengthen physician and reviewer relationships.
  • Enhance internal processes and improve overall operational performance and client satisfaction.

What Makes This Role Successful

Success in this role is defined by operational precision, strategic case ownership, and the ability to bridge the gap between complex legal deadlines and clinical expertise. You excel by quickly evaluating incoming referrals, accurately matching cases to the most qualified medical experts, and driving end-to-end delivery within strict turnaround times. By proactively auditing reports and testimony packages for first-pass legal accuracy, you ensure our deliverables consistently meet client standards and withstand jurisdictional scrutiny. You anticipate client needs, resolve service friction or fee discrepancies with poise, and adapt internal workflows to evolving statutory requirements. Ultimately, success means driving trust, and acting as a steady, solutions-oriented operator in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

What Your First 90 Days May Look Like

First 30 days

  • Learn Dane Street's Legal Services offerings, workflows, and case management processes.
  • Understand the counter affidavit process, client requirements, and jurisdictional guidelines.
  • Build relationships with clients, attorneys, adjusters, physicians, Sales, and internal teams.
  • Review existing documentation, quality standards, fee schedules, and operational procedures.
  • Identify workflow challenges and opportunities for improvement.

First 31-60 days

  • Independently manage assigned Legal Services cases and counter affidavit requests.
  • Coordinate qualified medical experts, reports, testimony, and depositions.
  • Serve as a primary Operations contact for clients and address service concerns.
  • Monitor case progress, turnaround times, outstanding deliverables, and quality.
  • Identify and resolve operational issues and billing discrepancies.
  • Recommend improvements to workflows and service delivery.

First 61-90 days

  • Demonstrate full ownership of Legal Services operations and the counter affidavit process.
  • Ensure accurate, complete, and timely deliverables.
  • Strengthen client and physician relationships and proactively resolve escalations.
  • Identify and implement opportunities to improve operational efficiency and quality.
  • Partner with Sales and leadership to support client retention and business growth.
  • Present recommendations for continued improvement and development of Legal Services.

Why Join Dane Street?

  • Collaborative remote culture
  • Professional growth opportunities
  • Meaningful work supporting the healthcare industry
  • Comprehensive benefits
  • Great Place to Work Certified since 2021
  • Commitment to employee development

Equal Opportunity Statement:

At Dane Street, caring for people is at the heart of what we do. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where every employee feels respected, valued, and empowered to contribute. We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees and make employment decisions based on qualifications, merit, business needs, and without regard to race, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Requirements

EDUCATION/CREDENTIALS:

Paralegal certification/ Medical certifications.

Must Haves:

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, professional judgment, discretion, relationship-building, and conflict-resolution skills.
  • Strong critical thinking and independent case assessment; ability to interpret complex instructions, recognize risks, and determine appropriate escalation.
  • Excellent organization, prioritization, time management, and follow-through across high-volume, deadline-driven work.
  • Working knowledge of clinical and legal review workflows, expert credentials, report quality expectations, and company service lines.
  • Ability to coordinate effectively across clients, physicians, attorneys, adjusters, Sales, Operations, Management, and Finance.
  • Previous experience in a healthcare, medical, legal, or insurance-related environment preferred. Relevant backgrounds may include clinical experience (such as CNA), legal support or administration, medical record review, medical transcription, medical documentation, or other healthcare operations roles.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • reviews, counter affidavits, depositions, testimony, or litigation support.

Employees receive basic life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage at no cost. Our generous paid time off policy ensures you have time to relax and recharge, while our 401k plan with a company match helps you plan for your future. Apple equipment and a media stipend are provided for remote workspace.

Executive Assistant


Help Finance leaders stay focused, prepared, and moving forward.


This is an opportunity to become a trusted partner to Resmed’s Finance Leadership Team, supporting leaders across the U.S. West Coast and Australia.


As Executive Assistant, you’ll go beyond traditional administrative support by helping leaders prioritize their time, prepare for critical discussions, coordinate leadership activities, and drive follow-through on decisions and commitments.


You’ll bring structure to a fast-moving global environment, connecting priorities, people, meetings, and information so leaders can focus on the work that matters most. From coordinating leadership rhythms and executive communications to global travel and offsites, you’ll help Finance leadership operate with clarity and consistency.


This role requires flexibility to adjust working hours to support leaders across U.S. West Coast and Australia time zones.


What You'll Do

  • Manage complex global calendars, aligning leadership time with high-impact priorities while anticipating conflicts, dependencies, and changing needs.
  • Build an understanding of Finance priorities, stakeholders, and business rhythms to anticipate needs, connect the dots and recommend practical solutions.
  • Coordinate Finance Leadership Team meetings, business reviews, planning sessions, offsites, and conferences, including agendas, pre-reads, stakeholder inputs, logistics, and materials.
  • Track decisions, actions, and key dependencies to create visibility, reinforce accountability and support follow-through.
  • Prepare executive communications, presentations, and leadership materials that are clear, organized, and appropriate for senior audiences.
  • Coordinate stakeholder inputs for external reporting, announcements, Board-related activities, and Investor Relations.
  • Partner across Finance, senior leadership, external stakeholders, and Resmed’s global Executive Assistant network to keep information and activities moving effectively.
  • Plan complex global travel, including itineraries and logistics, and manage related expenses.
  • Drive coordination for special projects and cross-functional initiatives involving multiple senior stakeholders, bringing structure to complex or ambiguous work.
  • Improve administrative and leadership processes using Microsoft 365, Copilot, automation, and emerging AI tools to simplify work and improve productivity.

What You Bring

  • Experience supporting senior executives or leadership teams in complex, global, high-pressure environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, complex schedules, and leadership team activities.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, with confidence engaging senior internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to anticipate needs, navigate ambiguity, solve problems independently, and exercise discretion, integrity, and sound judgment in sensitive situations.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365, including Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Excel, with effective use of AI tools such as Copilot.
  • Flexibility to adjust working hours to support U.S. West Coast and Australia time zones.

  • Experience in a global, publicly traded, healthcare, medical technology, or regulated environment.

What Sets You Apart

  • Anticipation: You look ahead, identify what leaders will need next, and act before competing priorities become obstacles.

  • Business Curiosity: You seek to understand the business behind the work, connecting priorities, stakeholders, and information to anticipate needs and become a more effective partner.

Why Join Resmed

At Resmed, your work helps enable a mission focused on helping people breathe better and live healthier, longer lives. You’ll work across a global Finance leadership environment, helping leaders operate effectively while shaping smarter ways of working through Microsoft 365, Copilot, automation, and emerging AI tools.

jobs.title: International Recruiter – European Customer Service Roles – Johannesburg
jobs.excerpt: Same time zone as Europe.  If you've worked agency or BPO desks on commission, you already know how this works, now paid per placement in euros.
jobs.description:
Same time zone as Europe. If you've worked agency or BPO desks on commission, you already know how this works, now paid per placement in euros. Open to recruiters based in Johannesburg and across South Africa.

Please read the whole post before applying. It's long on purpose. If it isn't for you, that's completely fine, and it saves us both time.

Who we are

BC Recruitment places people in jobs across Europe: multilingual customer service, sales and support roles with some of the biggest international employers, in cities like Athens, Lisbon, Porto, Braga and Sofia. Many of these jobs come with relocation help, which makes them easier to sell to candidates.

We have around 60 open roles right now, in Dutch, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Polish, Turkish, the Nordic languages and more. Alongside those we have specialist roles, like compliance, legal and tech, that pay a lot more per placement.

You don't need to speak the candidates' languages. Every role needs English, and English is what we work in. What matters is that you know where to find people and how to get them excited about a job abroad.

Who we're looking for

People who are hungry, driven and excited about this opportunity, and who believe they can earn more on commission than they do now.

We don't care how many years you've been recruiting. Someone with 6 months of hunger can beat someone with 10 years of experience. We care about what you have personally delivered: how many placements, for what kind of roles, and how many a month.

You'll probably fit if:

  • You're a natural seller who finds people on your own, without leads or hand-holding.
  • You understand that every nationality is found differently. If one channel doesn't work for a market, you know where those people really are and go there.
  • You already have your own tools: LinkedIn, laptop, phone, and whatever else you use to recruit.
  • You want freedom: your own hours, your own place, your own methods, no boss.
  • You have real numbers: placements or sales you made yourself, and you know your monthly average.
  • You've done global or international recruitment, ideally for similar companies or the same kind of candidates: customer service, call centres, multilingual roles, relocation, tourism, hospitality.

This is NOT for you if

  • You'll blame others when a client pauses a role or a candidate drops out. That's part of recruitment.
  • Most of the people you can reach need a visa. Most of our roles require candidates who can already work in the EU, and we don't offer visa support on most jobs.
  • You need a fixed income soon. There is no salary, retainer or paid trial at the start.
  • You need us to pay for tools before you can work. We don't cover anything at the start.
  • You want something to try "when you have time".
  • You need someone to tell you what to do every day.

What you earn

  • Minimum €400 per placement. Most roles pay €400–750, and specialist roles up to €2,400.
  • You see the exact payout on every role before you work on it.
  • A placement counts once your candidate has started and the employer has paid us. Someone who accepts and then drops out is not a placement.
  • Payment usually comes 1–3 months after your candidate starts, depending on the employer. We pay by bank transfer or whatever works for you.
  • Money you've earned is always paid. We know many recruiters are afraid of not being paid. Think about it from our side: a recruiter who delivers is worth far more to us over time than any single placement. This whole system is built on trust, and we'd lose by breaking it.

If you deliver, we deliver back

Nothing is given up front. For proven partners, things grow with your results, agreed case by case:

  • Once you deliver, we cover tool costs such as monthly subscriptions.
  • Proven recruiters can get earlier payouts, arranged with you.
  • Consistent performers can earn a monthly base on top of commission.

The rules bend toward the people who prove themselves. This job gets better the more you deliver.

What you get from day one

  • Proper onboarding: we explain everything, the employers, the roles and how we work, and answer all your questions before you start, so you begin with confidence.
  • Full role details and answers to the questions candidates usually ask.
  • You can reach us directly with any question about a role or a candidate.
  • Total freedom over how, when and where you work.

What's realistic

  • The first weeks are about building your pipeline.
  • Once you're up and running, a below-average recruiter makes about 1 placement a month, a good recruiter 2–5, and our best recruiters 5–10. It gets easier over time: you build a pool of candidates to come back to, and people start recommending you.
  • We expect at least one placement a month once you're up and running.

How we choose

  1. You answer the questions below. We read every answer.
  2. If your answers are strong, we have a video call.
  3. If we're a fit, we onboard you.

Everyone starts with a 30-day trial. Show real progress in that month, with candidates submitted and in interviews, and you stay and grow. If not, we part ways with no hard feelings.

To apply, answer these questions

  1. Your numbers. How many placements have you made per month on average, and for which roles and countries? What was your best month?
  2. The task. We have a Dutch-speaking customer service role in Athens, and candidates must already be allowed to work in the EU. Where exactly would you find 5 of them within two weeks, and how? Name the real channels, groups or searches you'd use.
  3. Commission. Why do you prefer being paid per placement over a salary, or over how you've been paid before?
  4. Your setup. Which tools and channels do you use today? How many hours a week can you put in, and what else are you working on right now?

Apply here with your CV. Then email your answers to , with your name and country in the subject. Applications without answers aren't reviewed.

Optional: attach a voice note or video answering "Why should we pick you?" It's the quickest way for us to get to know you.

Be specific: numbers, names, real examples. Answers that sound AI-written, or that just say what you think we want to hear, are rejected.

jobs.description:
Engineering Director

College Board – Technology 

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type:  Full-time position 


About the Team  

Team Observatory is a high-performing, self-organizing group of technologists focused on building and operating mission-critical score reporting systems and insights platforms that serve College Board’s Student community for CRA/AP Programs and the Bluebook platform. The work demands operational excellence, accuracy, and resilience at scale, while also requiring the team to continuously adapt to evolving business needs, technologies, and platforms. As College Board advances its 2027 strategy, this team is at the center of a multi-year transformation toward a consolidated, authentic Bluebook platform. The team balances the delivery of today’s critical capabilities with the exploration and adoption of new technologies, modern architectures, and AI-enabled solutions that will shape the future of score reporting.


About the Opportunity   

As an Engineering Director, you will lead a high-impact team responsible for delivering and operating systems that are foundational to College Board’s mission. This is an opportunity to lead in a dynamic, evolving environment where reliability, scale, and innovation must coexist.

You will guide your team through a changing technology and business landscape—balancing the demands of mission-critical score reporting with the opportunity to modernize platforms, adopt emerging technologies, and contribute to College Board’s long-term Bluebook strategy. You will be expected to deliver results today while helping position the organization for what comes next.


In this role, you are a catalyst and force multiplier: setting direction, removing obstacles, and enabling engineers to do their best work. You will bring clarity to ambiguity, translate strategy into execution, and build strong partnerships across product, architecture, data, and business teams. Your leadership will directly influence how College Board evolves its student score reporting capabilities into a scalable, secure, and unified platform. This role offers meaningful growth—for you and for the team. As College Board continues its journey toward a consolidated Bluebook platform, team scope, responsibilities, and technical challenges will evolve. You will play a key role in shaping that evolution while fostering a culture of learning, experimentation, and continuous improvement.


In this role, you will:  


Lead and Manage the team (40%) 

  • Lead a team of approximately eight engineers, responsible for building and operating student score reporting systems.
  • Set a clear vision and priorities for the team, track progress against goals, and provide coaching and feedback to support high performance and growth.
  • Foster an inclusive, high-achieving culture where team members are engaged, supported, and able to do their best work.
  • Build effective team structures and plan for evolving skill and capacity needs as product scope and platform strategy grow.
  • Develop and leverage the strengths of individual team members to deliver high-quality, scalable solutions using cloud and AI-enabled technologies.
  • Support diversity and inclusion across perspectives, skills, and experiences.
  • Consistently model College Board’s Operating Principles and Manager Expectations in daily leadership practices.

Strategic Partnership & Technical Communication (30%) 

  • Partner with business and technology stakeholders to clarify score reporting needs, constraints, and opportunities across student audiences.
  • Build trusted relationships with product, data, and engineering leaders to align priorities across complex, interdependent systems.
  • Communicate technical concepts clearly to diverse audiences, enabling informed decision-making and shared understanding.
  • Act as a technology partner in advancing AI-enabled capabilities that enhance score reporting, insights, and operational efficiency.
  • Drive engineering excellence through design reviews, shared standards, and constructive technical debate.
  • Balance scope, impact, and effort to deliver meaningful value while recognizing diminishing returns.
  • Collaborate closely with Solutions Architects, Senior and Lead Engineers, and Data Leads to evaluate features, estimate effort, and plan delivery.

Discovery, Definition & Delivery (30%) 

  • Develop a deep understanding of the business problems your team supports and translate them into clear technical direction.
  • Lead Agile (and post-Agile) delivery practices, ensuring clarity of priorities, disciplined execution, and sustained delivery momentum.
  • Guide technical decision-making by evaluating solution options, balancing tradeoffs, and acting as an arbiter when needed.
  • Partner with technology leaders to align architecture, cloud services, and delivery patterns with organizational goals.
  • Translate product and platform roadmaps into actionable plans, sequencing and prioritizing epics and stories with stakeholders.
  • Manage scope intentionally while identifying and reducing technical debt over time.
  • Monitor application cost and performance, partnering with internal teams to optimize efficiency and scalability.
  • Embed security and compliance considerations into all phases of design and delivery.
  • Ensure clean delivery and operational readiness, maintaining reliable services throughout their lifecycle.
  • Lead the identification, triage, and resolution of production issues to maintain system stability and reliability.
  • Continue to learn and keep abreast of developments in Generative AI software, sharing that knowledge within the team to support best practices

About You  

  • 10+ years of experience in software engineering, including building and operating secure, data-intensive, cloud-based systems.
  • Demonstrated success leading engineering teams to deliver complex products, services, or platform capabilities at scale.
  • Hands-on experience managing or owning web applications, ideally a user-facing portal, with a working knowledge of the security and infrastructure considerations that come with them, such as authentication, access controls, web application firewalls, and hosting environments.
  • Strong people-management experience, including coaching, performance management, and career development.
  • Proven ability to plan, prioritize, and execute in fast-paced, evolving environments.
  • Solid technical judgment with experience reviewing designs, guiding architectural decisions, and partnering with senior engineers.
  • Experience with modern cloud architectures; familiarity with AI integrations is a plus.
  • Ability to influence engineering strategy and decision-making across teams and leadership levels.
  • Calm, thoughtful leadership under pressure, with a focus on outcomes and continuous improvement.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to translate between business and technical contexts.

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, a performance exercise, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership, and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck — we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We're a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.


A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $140,000 – $175,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You'll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it's like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.

Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

This is a Stanford Health Care job.

A Brief Overview
Requires review of medical record documentation to accurately assign International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10-CM/PCS), as well as assignment of the Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) / All Patient Refined - Diagnosis Related Group (APR-DRG) and abstracts specific data elements for each account in compliance with federal and state regulations. This position codes the majority of patient types of inpatient records, including more complex cases such as Intensive Care. Follows the Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) Standards of Ethical Coding, as well as all American Hospital Association (AHA) Coding Clinic guidance. Follows Stanford Health Care policies and procedures and maintains required quality and productivity standards. Reviews, abstracts and assigns accurate and ethical ICD-10-CM/PCS codes to inpatient services. Ensures compliance with third party, State and Federal regulations. Reviews, analyzes and abstracts physician/other documentation for diagnoses, procedures, and other services provided. Obtains missing information and/or clarifies existing information. Completes volume of work from work queues per departmental productivity standards. Groups codes and completed product into payment group. Analyzes information for optimal and approprite reimbursement. Ensures compliance with all appropriate coding, billing and data collection regulations and procedures. Uses appropriate software to validate information. Utilizes Epic, 3M Coding and Reimbursement System (Encoder), 3M CDIS, 3M Audit Expert, MS Office, and other software as appropriate to compile and validate medical information.

Locations

Stanford Health Care

What you will do

  • Reviews medical record documentation and accurately assigns appropriate ICD-10 diagnosis and procedure codes, leading to the assignment of the correct Medicare Severity-Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) or All Patient Refined Diagnosis Related Group (APR-DRG). The Inpatient Coding Specialist II is responsible for verification of the patient's discharge disposition, assignment of the correct sources of admission for state regulation reporting purposes, and ensuring the appropriate present on admission (POA) indicators are assigned to each code. The assigned codes must support the reason for the visit that is documented by the provider in order to support the care provided.
  • Correctly abstracts required data per facility specifications.
  • Responsible for monitoring Discharged Not Billed accounts, and as a team, ensuring timely, compliant processing of inpatient accounts through the revenue cycle.
  • Collaborates with Clinical Documentation Specialists (CDSs) and members of the medical staff to ensure completeness of documentation in the medical records so that appropriate codes, and, ultimately, the correct Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) may be assigned.
  • Responsible for ensuring accuracy and maintaining established quality and productivity standards.
  • Demonstrates a high degree of independence in performance of responsibilities, working effectively without direct supervision. Exhibits strong time management, problem solving and communication skills.
  • Possesses critical thinking, good judgment and decision making skills.
  • Demonstrates excellent written and oral communication skills.
  • Remains abreast of current Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) requirements as well as Correct Coding Initiative (CCI) edits, Hospital Acquired Conditions (HACs), Patient Safety Indicators (PSIs), and when applicable, National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs,) including the addition of appropriate modifiers to ensure a clean claim the first time through.
  • Maintains competency and accuracy while utilizing tools of the trade such as the 3M encoder, 3M Audit Expert process (3M AES), 3M Clinical Documentation Improvement System (3M CDIS) and abstracting systems, as well as all reference materials.
  • Follows all established Stanford Health Care policies and procedures.
  • Attends required system, hospital and departmental meetings and educational sessions as established by leadership, as well as completion of required annual learning programs, to ensure continued education and growth.

Education Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or GED equivalent

Experience Qualifications

  • Five (5) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience

Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Successful completion of the Coder Proficiency Exam (pre-hire)
  • Ability to adapt to and deal with change and ambiguity
  • Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, work independently and meet deadlines
  • Ability to comply with the American Health Information Management Association’s Code of Ethics and Standards and apply Uniform Hospital Discharge Data Set (UHDDS) standards
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships
  • Ability to manage, organize, prioritize, multi-task and adapt to changing priorities
  • Ability to solve technical and non-technical problems
  • Ability to utilize the ICD-10-CM/PCS and CPT-4 coding conventions to code medical record entries; abstract information from medical records; read medical record documentation; assign accurate codes for grouping of MS-DRGs and APR-DRGs
  • Ability to work effectively through and with others
  • Knowledge of diagnosis/procedure DRG grouping schemes such as MS-DRGs and APR-DRGs
  • Knowledge of health information systems for computer application to medical records
  • Ability to foster effective working relationships and build consensus
  • Ability to work effectively with individuals at all levels of the organization
  • Knowledge of CCI (Correct Coding Initiatives) and CMS compliance issues
  • Knowledge of computer systems and software used in functional area
  • Knowledge of standards and regulations pertaining to the maintenance of patient medical records; medical records coding systems; medical terminology; anatomy and physiology and study of diseases

Licenses and Certifications

  • RHIA - Registered Health Information Administrator or
  • RHIT - Registered Health Information Technician or
  • CCS - Certified Coding Specialist

It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

Fullsteam is a leading provider of vertical software and embedded payments technology dedicated to helping businesses flourish by providing their customers with seamless experiences. With a dynamic and growing team of over 1,900 employees, we are committed to driving innovation and delivering best-in-class software and payment solutions that empower small and medium-sized businesses across numerous industries. Our purpose is to help our customers grow their businesses and delight their customers. Join us and be a part of a forward-thinking company that values growth, excellence, and the success of our clients.

The Senior People Business Partner (PBP) is a trusted advisor and hands-on partner to business leaders, helping them navigate people, performance, and organizational challenges in a dynamic and evolving business.


This role requires the ability to operate at both a strategic and tactical level -bringing sound judgment and business perspective to complex people decisions while also owning the execution required to move those decisions forward. The Sr. PBP will have particular responsibility for organizational effectiveness, performance management, and employee relations, while serving as a broader advisor to leaders on their teams and talent.


This role may support leaders and employees across both the United States and Canada, requiring familiarity with the different employment practices, regulatory environments, and employee relations considerations that apply across each country.

Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to business leaders, developing a strong understanding of their organization, priorities, talent, and challenges and translating business needs into practical people solutions.
  • Partner with leaders on organizational effectiveness, including team structures, roles and responsibilities, reporting relationships, workforce needs, and organizational changes.
  • Support leaders in evaluating talent and organizational decisions, considering business objectives, employee impact, cost, risk, and long-term effectiveness.
  • Lead the people-related planning and execution associated with organizational changes, ensuring decisions are thoughtfully implemented, communicated, and documented.
  • Coach leaders through performance management matters, helping establish clear expectations, providing effective feedback, addressing performance concerns, and determining appropriate next steps.
  • Develop and support performance improvement plans and related documentation when needed.
  • Lead and resolve employee relations matters, including employee concerns, workplace conflicts, policy issues, investigations, disciplinary actions, and other complex employee situations.
  • Conduct workplace investigations and provide clear, well-supported recommendations based on the facts, business context, applicable policies, and risk.
  • Help leaders distinguish between performance, capability, behavior, role clarity, organizational, and management issues to identify the right solution to a problem.
  • Provide candid counsel and constructive challenge to leaders, including when a different approach may better support the business or organization.
  • Partner with Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, People Operations, HRIS, Legal, and other People Team functions to execute solutions effectively.
  • Identify recurring themes or organizational challenges and recommend practical actions to improve leader effectiveness, employee experience, and business outcomes.
  • Support the implementation of broader People Team programs and priorities within assigned business areas.
  • Maintain strong ownership and follow-through, remaining engaged from initial assessment through successful execution and resolution.

Skills and Competencies:

  • Strong business acumen and the ability to connect people and organizational decisions to business outcomes.
  • Deep working knowledge of employee relations, performance management, and HR best practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to advise and influence leaders on complex and sensitive people matters.
  • Strong consultative and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify root causes, challenge assumptions, and develop practical recommendations.
  • Ability to assess risk thoughtfully and balance legal, employee, and business considerations.
  • Experience supporting organizational design, workforce planning, organizational change, and talent decisions.
  • Strong judgment and the ability to make effective decisions in situations that may be ambiguous or have competing considerations.
  • Ability to move comfortably between strategic consultation and detailed, hands-on execution.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to navigate difficult conversations effectively.
  • High level of ownership, discretion, and follow-through.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and sensitive matters in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
  • Proficiency with HCM systems; Workday experience preferred.

Experience and Education Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field; Master's degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of progressive HR experience, with a focus on business partnership and employee relations.
  • Experience supporting employees and leaders in both the United States and Canada strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of Canadian employment practices and provincial employment standards, with experience navigating employee relations, performance management, and organizational changes in a Canadian context strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience advising and influencing business leaders on complex people decisions.
  • Experience supporting organizational change, workforce planning, or organizational effectiveness initiatives preferred.
  • Experience working in a fast-paced, changing, or decentralized business environment preferred.
  • HR certification (e.g., SPHR, SHRM-SCP, CHRP, CHRL) is preferred.

Salary range: $100,000 - $110,000 USD

Fullsteam supports an inclusive workplace that values diversity of thought, experience, and background. Fullsteam is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, pregnancy, veteran status, marital status, creed, status with regard to public assistance, genetic status or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Contact Center Director
jobs.excerpt: InnovaCare Services Company, LLCThe Contact Center Director is the senior operational leader of InnovaCare's contact center, responsible for the performance, governance, culture, and strategic direction of the enterprise contact center function across all Central Florida markets (FCP/IPF, TMG/PFH, OFP).
jobs.description:
InnovaCare Services Company, LLC

The Contact Center Director is the senior operational leader of InnovaCare's contact center, responsible for the performance, governance, culture, and strategic direction of the enterprise contact center function across all Central Florida markets (FCP/IPF, TMG/PFH, OFP). This role provides direct executive-level oversight of all contact center operations — including omnichannel service delivery across voice, digital, and asynchronous channels; workforce management; quality assurance; technology governance; vendor management; and talent development — and serves as the primary operational accountability partner to the Executive Sponsor.

The Contact Center Director leads a team of three Market Managers, a Quality Manager, and a WFM & Business Systems Administrator, and is accountable for the performance outcomes produced by each function. This role also owns the governance relationship with the HGBPO after-hours vendor, including SLA compliance, contract oversight, and performance management.

This role represents a deliberate structural elevation from the current Contact Center Head/Lead position. The Director title reflects expanded scope, executive accountability, and the authority required to drive cross-market transformation, govern a multi-channel service environment, resolve structural barriers that have constrained performance, and operate as a credible peer to clinical and administrative leadership across InnovaCare's multi-brand environment.

The Contact Center Director does not manage individual agents directly. Strategic and operational decisions that require executive authority — budget approval, headcount expansion, vendor contract changes, or scope modifications — are escalated to the Executive Sponsor. All other operational decisions within the contact center are owned by this role.

Operational Leadership & Performance Governance

  • Own enterprise contact center performance across all markets and channels: establish, publish, and monitor KPI targets for service level (80/20 voice; channel-appropriate equivalents for digital), ASA, abandonment rate, AHT, digital response time, FCR, QA score, and schedule adherence — benchmarked against COPC CX Standard and SQM Healthcare standards
  • Convene and chair a weekly cross-market operations review with all three Market Managers: review prior-week performance data, resolve inter-market conflicts, surface systemic issues, and issue written decisions with accountability assignments — closing Governance Gap G-1
  • Establish a monthly executive reporting cadence to the Executive Sponsor: deliver a formal written operational summary covering KPI performance vs. benchmark, trend analysis, active initiatives status, risk register, and staffing posture — closing Governance Gap G-2
  • Implement and maintain a formal escalation governance framework: define escalation thresholds for patient complaints, QA fatal errors, SLA failures, and technology incidents; ensure all escalations are documented, assigned, resolved within defined SLAs, and reported — closing Governance Gap G-3
  • Build and maintain the contact center's operating calendar: annual planning cycle, initiative review rhythm, budget submission timelines, and QA calibration schedule — providing the governance structure that has been absent
  • Own the contact center's improvement roadmap: maintain a prioritized initiative register, sponsor active projects (including Dialpad migration, WFM setup, and AI deployments), and gate initiative launches using a formal prioritization framework — closing Governance Gap G-5

Team Leadership & Talent Development

  • Directly lead three Market Managers (FCP/IPF, TMG/PFH, OFP): conduct monthly 1:1 performance reviews, set individual development plans, and hold managers accountable for team-level KPI performance and agent engagement
  • Directly lead the Quality Manager: review monthly QA summary reports, approve program design changes, confirm calibration results are acted upon, and ensure QA independence is maintained across all markets
  • Directly lead the WFM & Business Systems Administrator: approve weekly staffing plans, review forecast accuracy results monthly, and ensure ACD configuration governance is maintained
  • Establish formal authority and accountability for the five Team Leads currently operating in an informal coaching-only capacity: define Lead scope of authority in writing, issue a Lead Handbook, and integrate Leads into the formal supervision and communication structure
  • Partner with HR to build a contact center talent strategy: define competency profiles for each role, implement structured onboarding for new hires (≥ 80 hours pre-live per COPC 2.06), and establish a succession and internal promotion pathway from Agent to Lead to Supervisor
  • Facilitate quarterly all-hands contact center communication: present organizational performance, strategic direction, and recognition — building engagement and organizational identity across the multi-market, multi-brand structure

Quality Assurance Oversight

  • Sponsor the enterprise QA program across all contact channels: approve the evaluation framework, calibration methodology, and fatal error criteria for both voice and digital interactions; ensure the program meets COPC 4.07 minimum standards (≥ 4 evaluations per agent per month) across all markets and channel types
  • Review the weekly QA dashboard and monthly enterprise QA summary delivered by the Quality Manager; issue written directives when QA scores fall below benchmark or when systemic patterns require structural intervention
  • Approve all remediation plans for agents scoring below threshold for two consecutive evaluation cycles; ensure Market Managers are accountable for coaching follow-through
  • Ensure QA findings are integrated into training content and Supervisor coaching practices; review training recommendations submitted by the Quality Manager and authorize action within 15 business days of submission

Workforce Management Oversight

  • Approve the weekly staffing plan and schedule produced by the WFM & Business Systems Administrator before publication; ensure plans reflect current market priorities and initiative impacts
  • Review forecast accuracy and adherence performance monthly; identify root causes of adherence gaps and assign corrective actions to the relevant Market Manager
  • Authorize overtime usage above threshold; maintain executive visibility to occupancy rate trends across markets; escalate chronic understaffing or overstaffing patterns to the Executive Sponsor with staffing recommendations
  • Own the HGBPO monthly headcount forecast submission (due by the 5th of each month per SOW §3(c)): confirm submission occurred, review forecast accuracy vs. actuals, and address discrepancies with HGBPO in writing

Vendor Management — HGBPO After-Hours

  • Serve as InnovaCare's primary contract authority over the HGBPO relationship: own SLA compliance monitoring, performance review cadence, and escalation management per the executed MSA (September 2025) and After-Hours SOW (effective October 1, 2025)
  • Chair the monthly HGBPO business review: review all contractual KPIs (SL%, abandon rate, CSAT, DSAT, schedule adherence, working rate), issue written performance notices for any metric below contractual target, and document all actions in the HGBPO performance log
  • Ensure all contractual oversight obligations are executed on time: confirm Daily Operational Summary receipt each morning, Monthly Business Review receipt by the 5th, and invoice reconciliation against Dialpad login/logout reports before approval
  • Escalate HGBPO contractual gaps to the Executive Sponsor and Legal: including the unexecuted HIPAA BAA, IP ownership clause (MSA §5(a)), absent termination-for-cause provision, and insurance deficiencies — and track remediation status
  • Maintain HGBPO operational readiness: confirm escalation contacts are current and reachable, urgent patient routing protocols are in place, and after-hours handoff procedures are documented and tested quarterly

Technology & Systems Governance

  • Serve as the operational authority for all contact center technology decisions: approve ACD configuration changes (queue, IVR, routing, skills) and digital channel platform changes before deployment; ensure no patient-facing system or channel configuration change is made without Director review and written approval
  • Own the active technology and channel initiative portfolio: Dialpad Contact Center migration, WFM module setup, CC Pods OFP, NovelVox/Athena pilot, digital channel enablement, and any AI feature deployments (Artera, Elise) — ensure each initiative has a named owner, timeline, and success criteria
  • Partner with the IT Lead and SVP IT on system integration priorities, uptime SLAs, and platform governance; represent contact center operational requirements in all technology decisions
  • Review the quarterly ACD configuration audit produced by the WFM & Business Systems Administrator; approve remediation actions for any discrepancy between documented and actual system configuration
  • Evaluate Dialpad AI feature maturity and readiness for deployment across all channels: approve or defer AI capability rollouts based on operational impact assessment for both voice and digital interactions; maintain a written AI governance log

Strategic Planning & Executive Engagement

  • Develop and maintain a 12-month contact center strategic plan, updated annually: headcount projections, omnichannel technology roadmap, quality maturity targets, digital channel expansion priorities, and HGBPO relationship evolution — aligned to InnovaCare's organizational growth
  • Produce the annual contact center operating budget: staffing costs, HGBPO vendor spend, technology licensing, training investment, and contingency; present to the Executive Sponsor for approval
  • Serve as the contact center's primary representative in cross-functional leadership discussions: participate in clinical operations reviews, patient experience committees, and technology governance forums as the voice of the contact center
  • Lead the contact center's participation in the FA-1 through FA-8 diagnostic assessment: serve as INT-01 (90-minute structured interview); ensure data submissions are complete, accurate, and delivered by deadline; implement findings from the improvement roadmap
  • Prepare and present quarterly business reviews to the Executive Sponsor: include performance vs. benchmark, transformation progress, risk register, and resource requests — in the executive format already established for the Company President

Innovacare participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.
